Pulse for 4 November 2026

The stories from 4 November 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Everyday tool

Codex deepens its review tools

Codex is OpenAI's coding product. OpenAI says it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, whose Trees and Diffs libraries the Codex app already uses to browse files and review changes, though the purchase has not closed.

Everyday tool

Spot AI fakes in images

Pangram Image 1.0 estimates whether a generator made a picture, or where those pixels sit inside a photo, and Pangram Image Flash 1.0 is the faster model the company aims at video.

Everyday tool

ChatGPT now makes GIFs

Images 2.6 is a new OpenAI image model, and as of 4 November 2026 ChatGPT can turn a text prompt or an uploaded photo into a short looping GIF.

Study

Cloud agents stop too early

CloudOpsBench is a new open-source benchmark that scores AI agents on cloud admin tasks, and the project says the usual failure is stopping early after a partial look.

AI agents

AI maps a hollow cell shell

A vault is a large hollow protein shell whose job is still unknown. Anthropic says Claude, under human direction, helped produce the first 3D cryo-EM map of one built from a phage protein in E. coli.

AI agents

Siri soon handles app tasks

An agent is a program that carries out steps for you, and Apple's developer preview lets any app hand Siri AI actions such as checking a delivery, while customers still wait and the feature is not offered in the EU on iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.

Everyday tool

Claude marks its own texts

A text watermark is an invisible pattern in word choice, and Anthropic says several Claude models now weave one in so eligible organizations can estimate whether Claude was likely involved, without learning who you are.

New model

Tencent's model can use PCs

Computer use is a model's ability to look at a screen and operate a computer, and Tencent says its new Hy4 can do that while the downloadable weights are not public yet.

Study

AI findings expire fast

The shelf-life project is a Stanford check of 50 widely cited findings about large language models, and the authors' trends put 22 of those findings in an expired zone by 30 September 2026.

AI agents

AI designed a test device

Astra is a model OpenAI used in an internal test to draft a simple device for talking to Codex, and the company says two team members still reviewed it before a factory built prototypes.
